Bus Bunching

You wait a long time for a bus. Then two turn up together. How can that happen on an evenly spaced route?

Imagine a few extra people waiting at one stop. Their bus takes longer to board them. During that delay, more riders arrive at the stops ahead. The following bus finds shorter queues, spends less time boarding, and catches up. That feedback is how buses bunch.

Watch a gap open

Press Play. Four buses circle twelve stops clockwise. In this run, passengers arrive at random and take rides of different lengths. Follow one bus and the gap behind it for a few laps. Pause or step back a minute to see where a pair first draws close.

What keeps the buses apart?

Give each stop one new passenger every twenty seconds, and give everyone a four-stop ride. Now each bus finds the same workload as its peers. They board, travel, and stop in step.

This is the route in equilibrium. The queues fill and empty, but the gap from one bus to the next stays at three stops for as long as the pattern repeats.

Try it. Choose Max speed and let hundreds or thousands of minutes pass. Pause at any point and check the largest gap.

Four seconds is enough.

Start with the same clockwork route. At 25:36, Bus 1 leaves Stop 8. For that one segment, its road travel takes 1.1 times as long: 44 seconds instead of 40. It then returns to its usual pace.

Four seconds can put an extra passenger at the door. Boarding that rider costs a little more time. The bus behind can catch up, leaving a wider gap behind itself. Farther back, another bus meets the queues that grew in that gap.

Follow the ripple. Watch Bus 1 after minute 25, then follow the other three. Which pair closes up first? Compare the gaps around minute 60 with the convoy around minute 90.

Can a dispatcher break up the bunch?

Holding a bus briefly can give the one ahead room to move. A delayed bus can regain ground by taking drop-offs only or announcing a pattern of skipped stops. Each choice changes who waits and for how long.

Try the recovery scenarios and compare the time passengers spend waiting and riding.
